analysis.title: GS Early Morning Research Recap: Ratings and Target Price Changes - November 6, 2026 as of 5:30 AM ET
key_insights: Three rating changes headline the recap. Keel Infrastructure (KEEL) is initiated at Neutral, with the data center pipeline opportunity offset by a limited track record. Kuehne & Nagel (KNIN.S) is cut from Buy to Neutral on reduced relative upside. Nantong Jianghai Capacitor (002484.SZ) is raised from Sell to Buy after a valuation reset.

Macro and global calls to focus on: Global Credit Trader (Lynam) outlines the directional risks from AI-related debt supply, and the Precious Analyst note (Thomas) is long-term constructive on gold but says 'just not today'.

The macro round-up lists the US Daily October Payrolls Preview (5 Nov) and the Global Economics Analyst on the 'fiscal cliff'. It also lists the Global PMI Monitor, which flags slowing manufacturing exports in Canada, and an India Strategy video on the India AI complex.

Data center demand is the dominant US equity thread. Notes cover US data center capacity forecast risks, how much runway is left in the data center construction cycle (Engineering & Construction), a KEEL initiation, a Watts Water raise on data center momentum, and IREN's F1Q27 review (EBITDA beat, favorable pricing, capex flexibility).

Energy and materials: MP Materials (Buy) posted strong results with record NdPr production and the start of magnet commercialization. NuScale (Neutral) has manufacturing progress but commercialization timing remains the key debate. Energy Fuels reported mixed uranium results while its rare earths platform advances on extended timelines. Devon beat on cash flow and is accelerating buybacks, with a debate likely on its Mid-Con hold.

Refiners and integrated oil: GS notes a positive rate of change on refining for Phillips 66. Marathon Petroleum stays Buy despite year-to-date outperformance. ExxonMobil is highlighted for downstream advantages and shareholder returns amid global volatility. Excelerate Energy's operational flexibility is said to solve its Hormuz risk. A LatAm energy note covers a sharp oil correction and revisits valuation and sensitivities.

Consumer staples and beverages: Monster (Buy reiterated) had a topline beat with EPS in line. Celsius (Buy reiterated) beat on both lines with growth likely to accelerate in 2027. Molson Coors had mixed Q3 results and lowered FY26 guidance on cost pressures. Primo Brands' cost pressures weigh on Q3 EBITDA and FY26 guidance. Kimberly-Clark's Q3 was in line and focus shifts to Kenvue (KVUE) integration.

Retail and apparel earnings reviews: Tapestry shows Coach durability with broad-based growth. Ralph Lauren outperformed in 2Q but Europe is an incremental worry. Kontoor gave initial FY27 guardrails with strong EPS growth but tempered revenue growth. FIGS and Savers Value Village had healthy results. Warby Parker's base business is uneven, with the Intelligent Eyewear launch as the next catalyst.

Gaming and leisure: Wynn Resorts (Maintain Buy) sees more headwinds than tailwinds this quarter, with UAE a key 2027 catalyst. Penn Entertainment stays Buy. Six Flags and United Parks stay Neutral, with 2027 growth described as a show-me story. Flutter's review is titled 'Resetting mid-term US profitability expectations'.

Fintech and payments: Affirm shows accelerating growth into the holiday season. Bill.com had a core revenue beat on strong take rate and volume trends. PAR Technology had a beat and raise. Shift4's weaker-than-expected preliminary 2027 guide weighs on the stock. Global Payments was relatively in line. NCR Voyix shares outperformed on an inflection in ACV. Allstate's 3Q26 EPS beat came from prior-year reserve development and net investment income, while its core auto loss ratio missed.

Internet and media: Airbnb's Q3 review reports raised FY26 expectations. Unity had a beat and raise driven by Vector. Lyft, Yelp, Grindr, Nextdoor and Genius Sports got constructive reviews. Mattel had mixed 3Q26 results driven by a one-time tariff benefit and lowered its 2026 guidance on weaker underlying trends. Live Nation stays Buy and focus shifts to its Investor Day. Sphere Entertainment had in-line results with lower estimates and target on softer Wizard of Oz outlook and content delays.

Healthcare and biotech: Allogene is set to present first autoimmune data at the American College of Rheumatology meeting this weekend. Intellia is tracking lonvo-z's US approval and hereditary angioedema launch in 1Q27. Sarepta's siRNA data in 4Q remains paramount. Revolution Medicines' Rasonque launch significantly exceeds expectations in its first 5 weeks. Zoetis faces an expected 4Q step-down that magnifies FY27 uncertainty. Agios awaits a sickle cell approval in early 2027.

Industrials and aerospace: General Dynamics remains Sell on SOTP and GAC margin trajectory. Joby is Sell. Beta Technologies is Buy. Eve Holding and Parsons are Neutral. Installed Building Products is called an attractive entry point. Primoris shows margin recovery on track with a strong initial 2027 framework.

Europe: Industrials and autos notes include Daimler Truck (large order miss, consensus EPS likely down low single digits), IAG (Q3 miss on disruption costs offset by stronger winter trading comments) and Amadeus (FY26 now expected at the lower end of guidance ranges). Next raised its price target and stays Buy. Utilities and mining notes cover EDP's incoming CEO, Gold Fields' Tarkwa uncertainty ahead of the Windfall FID and Lundin Mining's focus on the Vicuna FID.

Asia: Hon Hai's October revenue was in line at +46% YoY, with new AI servers, CPO switch and foldable phones expected to drive 4Q26. China Industrial Tech's 2027 outlook sees a valuation reset and prefers AI robotics and data center electricals over grid tech. China Property trip takeaways show cautious consensus on demand, with supply the primary driver of stability. Toyota's first disclosure of medium-term capital allocation was above expectations and its target was raised.

Gold equities: the Australia Metals & Mining note is cautious on gold equities near-term on margin and cash impacts. It names NEM, RMS and CMM as more defensive and cuts GMD to Neutral and RRL to Sell.

Sixteen US target price changes of 10% or more are listed. Large raises include EPAM to $140 from $100, Six Flags to $9 from $6, Angi to $9 from $6, NCR Voyix to $11 from $8 and Unity to $62 from $50. Cuts include Primoris to $81 from $92, Tronox to $3 from $4 and Genius Sports to $9 from $10.50.

Upcoming events: a US Internet earnings recap webinar with Eric Sheridan today at 11 AM ET, the 7th Annual Carbonomics Conference in London on November 10, and a European AI & Semis Symposium on November 24-25. Recent podcasts cover US midterm implications, the UK Budget and Brazil's post-election outlook.
